stories.headline: Tidal to ban fully AI-generated music from December 9
stories.summary: Tidal will stop allowing fully AI-generated music on December 9 and will delete roughly 27 to 29 million such tracks. It expects to reject about 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, while still accepting AI-assisted songs.
stories.why: Streaming platforms are setting content-provenance rules for AI output, which matters to anyone building generation, detection, or labeling tools.

sources.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming

stories.headline: Anthropic's MCP SDK passes 700 million monthly downloads
stories.summary: Anthropic reports over 700 million monthly downloads of its MCP SDK, two years after launch. It is adding background tasks, follow-up questions for users, and file uploads to let Claude work more autonomously.
stories.why: MCP adoption at this scale makes its new agent features a practical target for teams building tool integrations.

sources.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents

stories.headline: Google DeepMind lets AI agents run some Gemini experiments
stories.summary: DeepMind is using AI agents to run experiments for upcoming Gemini models. Research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says the lab is still far from recursive self-improvement, and it leaves the agents' chains of thought untrained so they can be reviewed.
stories.why: Agents running real research workloads raise practical questions about oversight and review that engineering leaders will face too.

sources.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant

stories.headline: Anthropic study finds many enterprise AI deployments deliver no value
stories.summary: An Anthropic study of nearly 300 AI deployments at 58 US companies found that about one in five delivers no business value. The main obstacles were heavy review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance, which the researchers link to outdated company structures.
stories.why: The findings point to process and organisational bottlenecks, not tooling, as the main reason AI rollouts stall.

sources.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools

stories.headline: Amazon reports hackers' AI agents exploited a zero-day with little human input
stories.summary: Amazon says attackers used AI agents to find and exploit a zero-day vulnerability with minimal human involvement. The report describes the Cairn AI framework as useful to both defenders and attackers.
stories.why: Autonomous exploit discovery shortens the window between disclosure and attack, so patching speed matters more.

sources.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input

stories.headline: Anthropic makes Claude Artifacts installable as desktop apps
stories.summary: Anthropic now lets users install Claude Artifacts as desktop apps on macOS and Windows, with a free account enough to do so. Users can build them in chat without writing code, and the apps can add menu bar items, send notifications, and create transparent windows.
stories.why: Turning chat-built artifacts into native apps lowers the barrier for building small internal tools without a developer.

sources.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows

stories.headline: Java4Shell: Oracle and OpenJDK ship fixes for a HotSpot Base64 decoder flaw
stories.summary: Oracle and the OpenJDK project released fixes on November 17 for CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the HotSpot JVM's Base64 decoder. JetBrains is urging users to update its IDEs and related tools.
stories.why: Any Java service or developer tool running an affected JVM may need patching now, and the bug sits in a widely used runtime component.

sources.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability: Update Your JetBrains IDEs, ReSharper, .NET Tools, Toolbox App, and Gateway Now

stories.headline: Active intrusion campaign targets Check Point security management servers
stories.summary: An ongoing intrusion campaign is targeting Check Point security management servers. The story drew substantial discussion on Hacker News.
stories.why: Management servers control security appliances across many networks, so a compromise there can expose a lot of downstream infrastructure.

sources.title: Active intrusion campaign against Check Point security management servers

stories.headline: AWS doubles Lambda maximum timeout to 30 minutes
stories.summary: AWS raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in and no new pricing. The limit had stood since 2018.
stories.why: Jobs that were split across functions or workflow steps only to fit the old limit may now run in a single invocation, which changes architecture choices.

sources.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
AWS Weekly Roundup: Local Zone in Bogotá, 30-minute Lambda timeout, and more (November 24, 2026)

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilises the never type after a decade of work
stories.summary: Rust 1.100.0, released on November 12, stabilises the never type (!) and makes Infallible an alias for it. It also stabilises the core of the allocator API and adds an opt-in dependency cooldown setting for Cargo.
stories.why: The cooldown setting lets teams delay pulling newly published dependency versions, a practical supply-chain control.

sources.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts

stories.headline: OpenAI details Pando, a Git backend built for concurrent coding agents
stories.summary: OpenAI described Pando, a new backend that scales Git for many concurrent coding-agent workloads while keeping standard Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency.
stories.why: Teams running many AI agents against shared repositories may hit contention, and this points to where the infrastructure load will show up.

sources.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando

stories.headline: Microsoft declares internal 'Code Red' after nearly 24-hour Outlook outage
stories.summary: Microsoft has declared an unusual internal 'Code Red' after a nearly 24-hour Exchange Online and Outlook outage this month. A bug on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers took email down for millions of customers.
stories.why: A single bug in shared networking infrastructure can take down a major service for a day, which is a useful reminder for anyone running large platforms.

sources.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage

stories.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets, including source code
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, including source code and proprietary technology from several companies. The BBC reports it was acquitted of racketeering charges.
stories.why: The verdict puts a spotlight on source code theft and how companies protect proprietary code from misappropriation.

sources.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
Huawei found guilty of stealing US trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
Jury finds Huawei stole US tech, laundered money, and broke sanctions
Huawei is guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, US jury rules

stories.headline: Matrix multiplication paper claims a Θ(n^2.25) bound and draws wide interest
stories.summary: A paper titled 'Matrix Multiplication is Θ(n^2.25)' has become a major discussion on Hacker News, with several hundred points and many comments. The item provides no further detail beyond the paper's title and reception.
stories.why: Matrix multiplication sits under many machine learning and numerical workloads, though real-world speedups depend heavily on constant factors.

sources.title: Matrix Multiplication is Θ(n^2.25) [pdf]

stories.headline: VMware ships third critical patch bundle in a week, including vCenter flaw
stories.summary: VMware has released its third critical patch bundle in a week, covering four more critical vulnerabilities. One of them is another unauthorised access flaw in vCenter.
stories.why: Teams running vCenter should prioritise these patches now, even with holiday change freezes getting in the way.

sources.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week

stories.headline: Australia nears passage of Digital Duty of Care Bill with large fines for platforms
stories.summary: Australian lawmakers are close to passing the Digital Duty of Care Bill, an amendment to the Online Safety Act 2021. The bill could result in massive fines for tech platforms.
stories.why: Platforms serving Australian users may need to review safety features, moderation and compliance processes before the law takes effect.

sources.title: Australia to pass safety bill that could result in massive fines for tech platforms

stories.headline: Claude-BugHunter repo trends with 84 skills for bug hunting and red-team work
stories.summary: A Python skill bundle for Claude Code aimed at bug hunting and external red-team work, with 84 skills and 15 slash commands. It gained about 1,800 stars today. Its coverage claims are not independently verified.
stories.why: It shows strong developer interest in AI agents for security testing, a dual-use area where teams should check scope and authorisation.

sources.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 84 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerabilit

stories.headline: CLI-Anything pitches agent-native command lines for all software
stories.summary: The project, titled "Making ALL Software Agent-Native", includes a CLI-Hub and gained about 1,070 stars today. It is trending rather than a proven standard.
stories.why: It reflects a push to make existing tools directly usable by AI agents, which could change how teams expose internal software.

sources.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

stories.headline: obra/superpowers, an agentic skills framework, adds about 1,000 stars today
stories.summary: The Shell-based project offers a framework of agentic skills and a software development methodology. It has about 326,000 stars in total and gained roughly 1,000 today.
stories.why: Its popularity shows where developer attention is moving: structured methods for coding agents rather than single prompts.

sources.title: obra/superpowers: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

stories.headline: Firecrawl pitches one API to search and scrape 550+ data providers for agents
stories.summary: The TypeScript project offers search, scraping and access to more than 550 data providers through a single API. It gained about 991 stars today.
stories.why: Data access layers for agents are a crowded, fast-moving category, so teams building agent pipelines may weigh build-versus-buy choices.

sources.title: firecrawl/firecrawl: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

stories.headline: Cursor publishes a plugin specification and official plugins on GitHub
stories.summary: The repository contains the Cursor plugin specification and official plugins. It gained about 360 stars today.
stories.why: A public plugin spec may become a format other editor and agent tools follow, which matters to teams writing extensions.

sources.title: cursor/plugins: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

stories.headline: JetBrains CEO predicts the end of manual code review within two years
stories.summary: JetBrains' CEO gives manual code review about two years before it fades, according to a LeadDev piece. The article asks whether human review of code is ending.
stories.why: If AI tooling takes over review, engineering leaders will need to rethink review policies, accountability, and how they train junior engineers.

sources.title: The end of manual code review?

stories.headline: LeadDev reports code ownership is eroding as developers trust AI more
stories.summary: A LeadDev article says less experienced developers place more trust in AI, and that code ownership is eroding as a result.
stories.why: Weaker ownership can make incidents harder to trace and review quality harder to maintain, so team leads need to address it directly.

sources.title: Code ownership is eroding

stories.headline: Cannabis users develop psychosis about 2.5 years earlier, with the gap widening with age
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 149 studies found cannabis users developed psychosis on average 2.5 years earlier than non-users. The gap grew to more than six years among adults aged 30 and older.
stories.why: Suggests cannabis-related psychiatric risk may build up over time, which is relevant to workplace wellbeing and health policy discussions.

sources.title: Cannabis users develop psychosis years earlier, and the gap grows with age

stories.headline: Childhood emotional abuse linked more strongly to adult mental illness than physical or sexual abuse
stories.summary: A Psychological Bulletin analysis of 104 studies found that childhood emotional abuse is associated with adult mental illness more strongly than physical or sexual abuse. The authors argue it is often underestimated because it leaves no visible marks.
stories.why: Points to emotional mistreatment as a serious harm, relevant to leaders shaping psychological safety and team culture.

sources.title: Childhood emotional abuse linked to adult mental health struggles more strongly than physical or sexual abuse

stories.headline: Pooled data from 362 studies examines how aging changes personality
stories.summary: Researchers pooled 362 studies covering nearly 400,000 people to test whether life makes personalities more alike or pushes them further apart with age. The item reports the question was tested but does not give the full answer.
stories.why: Provides a large-scale baseline on how personality shifts over a lifetime, useful context for long-term team planning.

sources.title: Psychologists pooled 80 years of data to answer a basic question about what aging does to our personalities

stories.headline: Ritalin reduces cheating in healthy adults when no one is watching
stories.summary: In a double-blind experiment, healthy adults given the ADHD stimulant methylphenidate cheated noticeably less when they were unobserved. This is a single study, so the result should be treated as preliminary.
stories.why: Shows that drug effects can extend beyond their intended use, a reminder to treat single experiments on performance enhancers with caution.

sources.title: Popular “smart drug” Ritalin unexpectedly curbs dishonesty in healthy adults

stories.headline: Dell beats earnings on AI server demand and authorizes $25 billion buyback
stories.summary: Dell's third-quarter overall sales more than doubled year on year, driven by demand for AI servers. The company also authorized a $25 billion share buyback.
stories.why: Strong AI server demand signals continued spending on AI infrastructure, which shapes hardware supply and pricing for teams running AI workloads.

sources.title: Dell earnings beat on AI strength, company authorizes $25 billion buyback
Dell in spotlight as Wall Street reacts to Q3 results, guidance analyst

stories.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump pressure, drawing scrutiny
stories.summary: Nvidia brought back CEO Jensen Huang, who had resigned after reports of multiple affairs, following pressure from President Trump. The move has intensified bipartisan scrutiny of tech companies' ties to the administration.
stories.why: Leadership instability at the largest AI chip supplier and rising political scrutiny could affect product roadmaps and access to Nvidia hardware.

sources.title: Trump’s meddling in Huang scandal reignites voter angst over tech’s outsized political power
Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is all alone in Washington

stories.headline: Lenders grow pickier on corporate bonds, making AI debt funding harder for Big Tech
stories.summary: Big Tech may find it increasingly difficult to raise funding from debt markets, which are critical to the AI build-out, as lenders become more selective over corporate bonds.
stories.why: Tighter credit for large cloud and AI providers could slow infrastructure expansion and influence the pricing and availability of AI platforms.

sources.title: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

stories.headline: Meta says its Muse AI agent is lifting ad business through Instagram
stories.summary: Meta does not show ads inside its Muse personal AI agent, but a senior executive told CNBC the tool is already boosting the company's advertising business.
stories.why: It shows how consumer AI assistants can feed revenue indirectly, which may shape how companies fund and prioritise their own agent products.

sources.title: How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent
